sources.title: Mauro Tosco, East Cushitic, The Oxford Handbook of African Languages (2020), author proof
sources.note: Institutional author proof indexed in full. Figure 21.1, printed page 292, places Somali within Omo-Tana and the larger Cushitic classification. Linguistic relationships do not establish one polity or map archaeological sites to named modern populations. Imported identity interpretation also rests on decoded geometry.

sources.title: González-Ruibal and colleagues, Nomads Trading with Empires: Intercultural Trade in Ancient Somaliland in the First to Seventh Centuries CE (2022)
sources.note: Original excavation report read directly in full. Xiis grave assemblages and trade analysis; earliest contexts are explicitly earlier than the imported seventh-to-tenth-century labels. No ethnic identity assigned from grave goods.

sources.title: Jorge de Torres, Towns in a Sea of Nomads, StateHorn project (20 October 2020)
sources.note: Excavating researcher’s illustrated project report read directly. Houses, mosques and querns belong to later medieval settlements, not automatically to 700 CE. The site’s boilerplate at the bottom is not source content.

sources.title: Jorge de Torres, My Road is Everywhere, StateHorn project (2021)
sources.note: Direct project report: Siyaara pottery tenth to sixteenth centuries, nomadic commerce, later Adal collapse. No claim of uninterrupted identical institutions throughout two millennia.

sources.title: Jorge de Torres, Harsh and Challenging, StateHorn project (2020)
sources.note: Project synthesis of regional geography and historically documented seasonal pastoral movement, rain and shallow wells. Used as dated later evidence, not a recovered family diary from 700.

sources.title: British Museum, milk pot Af1935,1108.63.a
sources.note: Official collection entry indexed; direct fetch failed. Wooden vessel with woven vegetable fibre and knobbed lid; 1934 to 1935 Powell-Cotton field collection from southern Somalia. Acquisition date is not a precise manufacture date.

sources.title: British Museum, Issa head-rest Af1913,0616.48
sources.note: Official collection entry fully indexed. Carved wooden head-rest, conical base, Somalia, circa 1910 to 1912, height 14.5 cm; collected by Louis Clarke.

sources.title: British Museum, Object Journeys (2016)
sources.note: Official museum report fully indexed; direct access failed. Ten young London Somali adults in 2015 to 2016 worked with museum collections. Photograph caption documents handling and trying a head-rest; no universal sleeping custom inferred.

sources.title: Unicode Standard 17.0, Chapter 19, section 19.2: Osmanya
sources.note: Direct text witness provides the exact encoded sample and English gloss. Only this short passage charged here because the same chapter is already cited by other atlas cards. The source’s 1973 orthography date is not used.

sources.title: Michael Everson, interview on the Osmanya encoding project (2002)
sources.note: Participant’s own account, questions 3 to 5: family photocopy, 1999 first proposal, collaboration with Osman Abdihalim Osman Yusuf Keenadiid and 2001 final proposal. Future publication forecasts are not treated as completed events.

proposedOverrides.summary: A regional history of communities in the Somali Horn, with clearly dated archaeological and later examples.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Shared phased regional card justified by matching broad Somali-Horn geography and variant linguistic labels, not an asserted historical kingdom or identity with Nile Kush. Neither bounds nor labels identify the language of every excavated community. Explicitly earlier Xiis and later medieval/modern witnesses.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact Unicode Osmanya phrase, translated and dated to modern script tradition. No invented seventh-to-tenth-century Cushitic inscription.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: The archaeological case studies emphasize the northern part of the imported region, while the milk vessel gives a separately dated southern Somali household example. The broad polygon is not a precise ethnic boundary.
